# Settings

Every setting lives under `readMarkdown.*`. Open the Settings UI (`Ctrl+,`) and search for "Read Markdown", or edit `settings.json`.

- **⚙** marks a setting you can also change from the quick settings panel (⚙ in the preview toolbar). The panel writes to the most specific scope that already defines the setting (folder, workspace or user).
- **🔒** marks a setting that workspace settings cannot change until you trust the workspace ([Security](Security)).
- An invalid value falls back to the default, and a number out of range is clamped to it.

## Preview

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readMarkdown.preview.replaceDefault` | boolean | `false` | Use Read Markdown for `Ctrl+Shift+V` / `Ctrl+K V` instead of the built-in Markdown preview. |
| `readMarkdown.preview.autoOpen` | string | `"off"` | Automatically open the preview when a Markdown file is opened.<br><br>Values: `off`: Do not open the preview automatically.<br>`beside`: Open the preview beside the editor when a Markdown file is opened.<br>`active`: Open the preview in the same editor group when a Markdown file is opened. |
| `readMarkdown.preview.scrollSync` | boolean | `true` | Synchronize scrolling between the Markdown source and the preview. |

## Quick navigation

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readMarkdown.nav.show` ⚙ | boolean | `true` | Show the quick navigation sidebar (headings outline). |
| `readMarkdown.nav.position` ⚙ | string | `"left"` | Position of the quick navigation sidebar.<br><br>Values: `left`<br>`right` |
| `readMarkdown.nav.maxDepth` ⚙ | integer | `3` | Deepest heading level shown in the quick navigation.<br><br>Range: min 1, max 6. |
| `readMarkdown.nav.width` | integer | `260` | Width of the quick navigation sidebar in pixels. You can also drag the sidebar edge in the preview (double-click it to reset).<br><br>Range: min 120, max 600. |

## Theme

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readMarkdown.theme.preset` ⚙ | string | `"vscode"` | Base color preset. Individual color settings override it.<br><br>Values: `vscode`: Follow the current VS Code color theme.<br>`light`: Light paper-like theme.<br>`dark`: Dark theme.<br>`sepia`: Warm sepia theme, easy on the eyes for long reads.<br>`high-contrast`: High contrast theme. |

## Body text

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readMarkdown.body.fontFamily` | string | `""` (unset) | Font family for body text. Empty uses the preset default (system UI font). |
| `readMarkdown.body.fontSize` ⚙ | number | `15` | Body font size in pixels.<br><br>Range: min 8, max 40. |
| `readMarkdown.body.lineHeight` ⚙ | number | `1.65` | Body line height (unitless multiplier).<br><br>Range: min 1, max 3. |
| `readMarkdown.body.maxWidth` ⚙ | integer | `860` | Maximum content width in pixels. 0 means full width.<br><br>Range: min 0. |
| `readMarkdown.body.fullWidth` ⚙ | boolean | `false` | Let the content fill the whole preview width, ignoring `readMarkdown.body.maxWidth`. |
| `readMarkdown.body.backgroundColor` | string | `""` (unset) | Background color (any CSS color). Empty uses the preset. |
| `readMarkdown.body.textColor` | string | `""` (unset) | Text color (any CSS color). Empty uses the preset. |

## Headings

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readMarkdown.headings.fontFamily` | string | `""` (unset) | Font family for headings. Empty uses the body font. |
| `readMarkdown.headings.scale` ⚙ | number | `1` | Multiplier applied to all default heading sizes.<br><br>Range: min 0.5, max 3. |
| `readMarkdown.headings.fontSizes` | object | `{}` | Per-level font size overrides as CSS values, e.g. `{ "h1": "2.4em", "h2": "22px" }`. Overrides `headings.scale`.<br><br>Keys: `h1`, `h2`, `h3`, `h4`, `h5`, `h6`. |
| `readMarkdown.headings.colors` | object | `{}` | Per-level heading colors, e.g. `{ "h1": "#d73a49", "h2": "#005cc5" }`.<br><br>Keys: `h1`, `h2`, `h3`, `h4`, `h5`, `h6`. |
| `readMarkdown.headings.highlight` ⚙ | string | `"underline"` | Visual highlight style for H1/H2/H3 headings.<br><br>Values: `none`<br>`underline`<br>`background`<br>`leftBorder` |
| `readMarkdown.headings.highlightColor` | string | `""` (unset) | Color used by the heading highlight style. Empty uses the preset accent color. |

## Custom CSS

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readMarkdown.customCss.inline` 🔒 | string | `""` (unset) | Custom CSS appended after all built-in styles. |
| `readMarkdown.customCss.files` 🔒 | string[] | `[]` | Paths to CSS files (absolute, or relative to the first workspace folder) appended after built-in styles. Files are watched for changes. |

## Search highlight sync

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readMarkdown.search.syncSelection` | boolean | `true` | Highlight the text selected in the Markdown source (including matches you step through with the Find widget, `Enter`/`F3`) in the preview. |
| `readMarkdown.search.caseSensitive` | boolean | `false` | Match highlighted text case-sensitively. |
| `readMarkdown.search.minLength` | integer | `2` | Minimum selection length that triggers highlighting.<br><br>Range: min 1. |
| `readMarkdown.search.highlightColor` | string | `""` (unset) | Background color of matches. Empty uses the theme find-match color. |
| `readMarkdown.search.currentHighlightColor` | string | `""` (unset) | Background color of the current match. Empty uses the theme current find-match color. |

## Mermaid diagrams

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readMarkdown.mermaid.enabled` | boolean | `true` | Render ```mermaid code blocks as diagrams. |
| `readMarkdown.mermaid.theme` ⚙ | string | `"auto"` | Theme of Mermaid diagrams. Themes with a dark variant switch to it when the preview is dark.<br><br>Values: `auto`: Colored like the preview (theme preset, custom colors, VS Code theme), without gradients.<br>`default`: Mermaid's default theme; its dark theme in a dark preview.<br>`neo`: Mermaid's neo theme; neo-dark in a dark preview.<br>`redux`: Mermaid's redux theme (monochrome); redux-dark in a dark preview.<br>`redux-color`: Mermaid's redux-color theme; redux-dark-color in a dark preview.<br>`base`: Mermaid's base theme with its own colors (light only).<br>`forest`: Mermaid's forest theme, greens (light only).<br>`neutral`: Mermaid's neutral theme, greys for printing (light only). |
| `readMarkdown.mermaid.look` ⚙ | string | `"classic"` | Drawing style of Mermaid diagrams.<br><br>Values: `classic`: Mermaid's classic shapes.<br>`neo`: Mermaid's newer, cleaner shapes (pairs well with the neo and redux themes).<br>`handDrawn`: Sketch-style shapes. |

| `readMarkdown.sections.collapsible` | boolean | `true` | Allow collapsing the content under each heading. |

## Editing in the preview

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readMarkdown.edit.enabled` ⚙ 🔒 | boolean | `false` | Edit the Markdown source of a block (paragraph, heading, list, table, code block, front matter) directly in the preview: hover a block and click ✎. Task list checkboxes become clickable and toggle `[ ]` / `[x]` in the source directly. `Ctrl+Enter` / `Cmd+Enter` saves the block, `Escape` cancels. Edits go through the normal undo stack. |
| `readMarkdown.edit.doubleClick` ⚙ | boolean | `false` | Also open a block for editing by double-clicking it. Only applies when `readMarkdown.edit.enabled` is on. |
| `readMarkdown.edit.saveOnCommit` 🔒 | boolean | `false` | Save the file after each block edit made in the preview. Files not open in any text editor are always saved, so edits are never left in an invisible unsaved buffer. Only applies when `readMarkdown.edit.enabled` is on. |

## Changes against git

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readMarkdown.changes.mode` ⚙ | string | `"inline"` | Show how a git-tracked file differs from its staged (git index) version, like the change bars in the editor gutter. Clicking a file in the Source Control view still opens VS Code's text diff. The preview's ± toolbar button switches between `inline` and `gutter` for that preview.<br><br>Values: `inline`: Track changes in the text: removed text struck through in red, added text in green, moved blocks double-struck in red where they were and double-underlined in green where they are now (joined by a yellow arrow), plus change bars beside the text.<br>`gutter`: Only change bars beside the text (green added, blue modified, red removed, green moved).<br>`off`: Do not show changes. |

## Task lists and agent progress

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readMarkdown.tasks.agentProgress` ⚙ | boolean | `true` | Follow an AI agent working through a plan: task items marked in progress with `- [/]` (also `[~]`, `[-]`) are highlighted with an animated “working” label, the preview scrolls to each step as it starts, and a step flashes when it is checked. When off, `[/]` is shown as plain text, as on GitHub. |
| `readMarkdown.tasks.progress` ⚙ | boolean | `true` | Show a progress bar for task lists (done, in progress, open) and done/total counts beside outline headings. Only applies when `readMarkdown.tasks.agentProgress` is on. |

## Security

| Setting | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readMarkdown.security.allowRemoteContent` 🔒 | boolean | `true` | Allow the preview to load remote (`https:`) images and media, including ones requested from a document's CSS. When off, only images and media from your workspace, the document's folder and `data:` URIs are shown, so opening a document cannot reveal your IP address or that you opened it. Remote stylesheets and fonts (for example `@import url(https://…)` in a document or in custom CSS) are always blocked. Applies to open previews right away; an unsaved in-preview block edit is discarded when the preview reloads. A workspace cannot change this setting until it is trusted. |

## Example

```json
"readMarkdown.theme.preset": "sepia",
"readMarkdown.body.fontFamily": "Georgia, serif",
"readMarkdown.headings.colors": { "h1": "#8b4513", "h2": "#a0522d" },
"readMarkdown.customCss.inline": ".rm-markdown p { text-align: justify; }"
```

More styling in [Custom CSS](Custom-CSS).
